claims: A Super El Niño is an exceptionally strong warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
A Super El Niño is often defined as sea surface temperatures rising 2°C or more above average.
Forecasters are monitoring a potential Super El Niño for 2026-2027.
Super El Niño is not a technical term.
Super El Niño is used by scientists to describe high-intensity El Niño events.
High-intensity El Niño events are similar to those in 1982-83, 1997-98, and 2015-16.
Forecasts suggest a 1-in-3 chance of a Super El Niño event by late 2026.
A moderate-to-strong El Niño event is more certain.
There was a recent La Niña.
